checks.claim: ECMS: outlay Rs 22,919 crore; Cabinet approval 28 Mar 2025; notified 8 Apr 2025; 6-year tenure plus optional 1-year gestation; targets Rs 59,350 crore investment and 91,600 direct jobs
checks.corrected_value: Outlay, Cabinet date, tenure and targets confirmed. Two additions: the scheme also targets production of Rs 4,56,500 crore, and the capex incentive runs 5 years (the 1-year gestation applies to the turnover-linked incentive). The Cabinet-approval PIB release is PRID 2116172 (the research file cites PRID 2222519, which is a different, later release). The '8 Apr 2025' notification date could not be independently pinned (a News On AIR item 'Centre notifies Rs 22,919 cr electronics component scheme' exists but its date was not visible) - unverifiable (search budget).
checks.evidence: PIB (PRID 2116172) 'Cabinet approves Electronics Component Manufacturing Scheme' states the Rs 22,919 crore outlay and that the scheme 'envisages to attract investment of Rs 59,350 crore, result in production of Rs 4,56,500 crore and generate additional direct employment of 91,600 persons'; Vision IAS/Organiser date the approval to 28-29 Mar 2025. Drishti IAS and Manorama Yearbook both describe a six-year tenure with a one-year gestation for the turnover-linked incentive and a five-year capex incentive.

checks.claim: ECMS approvals to date: 31 proposals worth Rs 7,877 crore cleared as of 17 Aug 2026
checks.corrected_value: 31 proposals / Rs 7,877 crore is only the tranche approved on 17 Aug 2026 (IT Secretary S Krishnan), not the cumulative total. Cumulative approvals rose from 7 projects (Oct 2025) to 75 and then 106 projects as of 17 Aug 2026; a News On AIR item of 30 Mar 2026 put 75 projects at Rs 61,000 crore of investment. The scheme has drawn Rs 1.15 lakh crore of proposals across 249 applications (roughly double the Rs 59,350 crore target). The Aug-2026 tranche spans 10 states, is expected to yield Rs 82,243 crore of production and ~10,000 jobs, and includes Syrma SGS, Centum Electronics, Sensata, GX Group, Rosenberger, Globe Capacitors and Britannia RFID.
checks.evidence: Business Standard (17 Aug 2026), ETV Bharat, ThePrint, Deccan Chronicle and Swarajya all report the 31 fresh proposals worth Rs 7,877 crore; Business Standard adds that approvals 'have been cleared in tranches, rising from seven projects in October 2025 to 75 ... and 106 on Monday'. Deccan Herald reports Rs 1.15 lakh crore of investment proposals from 249 applications; News On AIR (30 Mar 2026) reports 75 projects worth Rs 61,000 crore approved.

checks.claim: PMP: 20% basic customs duty on imported finished smartwatches (and hearables) under the Budget 2022-23 Phased Manufacturing Programme
checks.corrected_value: 20% BCD on HS 8517 62 90 (smart watches), plus 10% Social Welfare Surcharge on the BCD and 18% IGST on the cumulative value - i.e. an all-in import levy of roughly 44% before any concession. CESTAT Delhi has held smart watches classify under 8517 6290, not 9102 (wrist watches). Global Trade Alert records the PMP for wrist wearable devices as Notification No. 11/2022-Customs of 1 Feb 2022.
checks.evidence: CusBuzz tariff database lists BCD 20.00% and AIDC 0% for HSN 85176290, with 10% SWS and 18% IGST on top; TaxGuru reports the CESTAT classification ruling; Global Trade Alert (state act 62058) documents the PMP notification.

checks.claim: PMP component duty ladder: wearable/hearable components at 0-15% BCD stepping up across FY23-FY26, most components nil from 1 Apr 2022
checks.corrected_value: The instrument is confirmed but the rate table is not: Notification No. 11/2022-Customs (1 Feb 2022, effective 1 Apr 2022) sets a graded BCD structure for 'wrist wearable devices (commonly known as smart watches) and other smart wearable devices including smart rings, shoulder bands, neck bands or ankle bands' and their PCBA, battery and charging cable, and was amended by Notification 33/2023-Customs ('Graded BCD structure for hearable/wearable devices and its parts, sub-parts and subassembly'). The per-item, per-year 0-15% values were not retrieved before the search budget ran out (search budget). Note for FitForge: a screenless band is explicitly within the notification's scope.
checks.evidence: TaxTMI lists Notification 33/2023-Customs as an amendment to 11/2022 and 12/2022 establishing the graded BCD structure for wearables and parts; howtoexportimport.com carries the text of 11/2022 covering PCBA, battery and charging cable for wrist wearable devices effective 1 Apr 2022; Global Trade Alert confirms the PMP. No source retrieved shows the year-by-year percentage ladder.

checks.claim: BIS CRS on the device under IS 13252 (Part 1):2010 is mandatory for smartwatches; migration to IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 with deadline 1 Nov 2028
checks.corrected_value: Confirmed, with additions: smart watches have been under CRS/IS 13252 (Part 1):2010 since 23 May 2018; BIS implementation guidelines run IS 13252 (Part 1):2010 and IS 616:2017 concurrently with IS/IEC 62368-1:2023 until 1 Nov 2028, after which the old standards are withdrawn and no new registrations under them are accepted; BIS published a migration FAQ in Jul 2026. Caveat: confirmation is by consensus of 7+ certification consultancies (Aleph India, EVTL, Compliance Calendar, Diligence, Swarit, Elitas, SIQ, MPR, BL India, C-PRAV); no BIS/MeitY primary page was retrieved (search budget).
checks.evidence: Aleph India: 'From 23 May 2018, BIS has required SMART WATCHES to be registered as per IS 13252 (Part 1):2010 under Compulsory Registration Scheme'; SIQ, MPR India Certification, EVTL, BL India and C-PRAV (BIS FAQ, 27 Jul 2026) all state the transition window ends 1 Nov 2028, when IS 13252/IS 616 are withdrawn in favour of IS/IEC 62368-1:2023.

checks.claim: WPC Equipment Type Approval by self-declaration on Saral Sanchar at Rs 10,000 per product, processed in 1-3 working days
checks.corrected_value: Fee confirmed: Rs 10,000 per model, paid via Bharatkosh, application only through Saral Sanchar (mandatory since 1 May 2019); ETA-SD covers de-licensed bands incl. Bluetooth 2.4 GHz and needs an RF test report plus manufacturer authorisation. The '1-3 working days' processing time appears only in consultancy blogs and was not independently confirmed (search budget).
checks.evidence: Bureau Veritas CPS newsroom describes the WPC Wing's ETA-through-self-declaration on the Saral Sanchar portal; the DoT eServices portal has a dedicated 'WPC - ETA (Self Declaration)' page; Professional Utilities and Standphill both state the government fee is Rs 10,000 per model paid through Bharatkosh.

checks.claim: boAt UDRHP (Oct 2025): 75.83% of units made in India in Q1 FY26 vs 39.65% in FY23; >75M units made domestically; Califonix (50:50 Dixon JV) made 13.44M units in FY25 at 44.80% utilisation of 30M installed capacity; 3.19M units = 37.46% of boAt units in Q1 FY26; wearables Rs 330.41 crore = 10.76% of FY25 revenue
checks.corrected_value: Localisation and Califonix figures confirmed against multiple reports of the UDRHP-1 (75M units is 'as of 30 June 2025'). The wearables-revenue line (Rs 330.41 crore / 10.76%) was not independently re-verified (search budget).
checks.evidence: Business Standard (21 Nov 2025): boAt 'transitioned 75.83 percent of total production to domestic facilities in Q1 FY26, up from 39.65 percent in FY23' and Califonix 'manufactured 13.44 million units, translating into a robust 44.80 percent capacity utilisation against an annual installed capacity of 30 million units', with 3.19M units (37.46%) in Q1 FY26; Inc42, Manufacturing Today India and Indian Retailer carry the same UDRHP figures.

checks.claim: Dixon Q1 FY26: wearables & hearables segment revenue INR 175 crore for the quarter
checks.corrected_value: Confirmed. Context: Q1 FY26 consolidated revenue Rs 12,838 crore (+95% YoY), PAT Rs 280 crore (+100%); telecom Rs 1,410 crore, IT hardware Rs 247 crore, hearables & wearables Rs 175 crore.
checks.evidence: Yahoo Finance's Q1 2026 earnings-call highlights and AlphaStreet both report 'Wearables & Hearables Revenue reached INR 175 crores in Q1 FY26' alongside the segment breakdown; Business Standard confirms the Rs 280 crore PAT.

checks.claim: IDC 2025 full year: India wearables 114.2M units (-4.0% YoY, second annual decline); smartwatches 28.9M (-17.6%); smartwatch ASP USD 26.5 (from USD 23.8, +11.7%); overall wearables ASP USD 20.3 (+1.8%)
checks.corrected_value: Unit, decline and smartwatch-ASP figures confirmed by IDC's own channel. Additions: earwear 84.7M units (+1.4%); smart glasses +1,541.3%; realme +27.8%. The overall-wearables ASP of USD 20.3 was not visible in any retrieved snippet (search budget).
checks.evidence: IDC Asia/Pacific's official X post: 'India's wearable market fell 4.0% YoY to 114.2M'; The Tech Outlook, FoneArena, Communications Today and Beebom quote the IDC release: smartwatches fell 17.6% to 28.9M while ASPs rose 11.7% from USD 23.8 to USD 26.5.

checks.claim: Counterpoint: domestic-manufacturing share of India smartwatch shipments reached 82% in Q3 2023 (from 4% a year earlier); Q2 2025 smartwatch shipments fell 27% YoY (fifth straight quarterly decline; Q1 2025 -33%), with Noise + boAt + Titan/Fastrack at 62% combined share
checks.corrected_value: Both Counterpoint figures confirmed on Counterpoint's own pages (Q3 2023 shipments also grew 21% YoY; Noise held 34% share in Q2 2025). The Q1 2025 '-33%' figure was not re-verified (search budget). Note the 82% localisation datum is three years old and no newer localisation share was found.

checks.claim: FX: Rs 85 per USD used for all USD conversions (implied by Aug-2026 coverage converting Rs 22,919 crore to ~USD 2.7B; inside the Rs 83-90 band)
checks.corrected_value: USD/INR was ~95.7-95.8 on 14 Sep 2026 (BookMyForex 95.72; Trading Economics 95.834, +0.25% d/d; rupee down 8.75% over 12 months). Rs 85 is the Mar-2025 rate embedded in the original USD 2.7B conversion and is ~12% stale; the prompt's Rs 83-90 band is also stale. Re-based examples: ECMS Rs 22,919 crore = ~USD 2.39B; Rs 59,350 crore = ~USD 6.2B; WPC fee Rs 10,000 = ~USD 104; Dixon Q1 FY26 W&H Rs 175 crore = ~USD 18.3M.
checks.evidence: Search results dated 14 Sep 2026 give 1 USD = 95.72 INR (BookMyForex) and 95.834 (Trading Economics), with the rupee down 8.75% over the past 12 months; the Federal Reserve H.10 release of 8 Sep 2026 is listed as a primary series to pull the exact reference rate.

checks.claim: India tooling NRE: injection-mould tooling Rs 2 lakh to Rs 30 lakh+ per tool (Moldrite 2026); jigs/fixtures Rs 60,000 to Rs 6 lakh (IndiaMART)

The jig/fixture range is a marketplace listing. Treat both as indicative only; a wearable needs ~3-5 tools (housing, optical window/back, strap/buckle, charger) - that count is unsourced.
checks.evidence: Moldrite (2026): 'Injection molding cost in India typically ranges from Rs 2 lakh to Rs 30 lakh+ for tooling'; Sensio-AI notes TPU is typical for straps; no independent Indian source with a comparable tooling range was retrieved.

GAP (a) Per-unit EMS conversion / box-build charge for a wearable in India: NOT FOUND after 2 further searches this session (14 in the prior session). Only generic non-India figures surfaced - QueenEMS box-build USD 50-150/unit for 'simple' builds (https://www.queenems.com/blog/box-build-assembly-complete-guide-from-pcba-to-finished-product/) and SMT USD 50-500/board at prototype volume (https://smtassemblycost.com/), neither applicable to a sub-USD-30 band - plus an IndexBox paid-report blurb that Dixon and Syrma SGS run module-level smartwatch chipset assembly lines (https://www.indexbox.io/store/india-smartwatch-chips-market-analysis-forecast-size-trends-and-insights/). Only triangulation available (my inference, not a source): Dixon Q1 FY26 wearables+hearables revenue Rs 175 crore against Califonix's 3.19M units in the same quarter caps EMS revenue at roughly Rs 550/unit - and that would include materials if Dixon buys the BoM, so pure conversion is a fraction of it. Two further searches (Dixon per-unit realisation; ICEA/ELCINA value-add benchmarks) were blocked by the search budget. Must come from RFQs (Dixon, Optiemus, VVDN, Syrma SGS, East India Technologies).

GAP (b) Indian design-services rates (VVDN, Tata Elxsi, Sasken, Mistral): NO RATE CARD FOUND. Proxy found: Tata Elxsi FY25 operating revenue Rs 3,729 crore (company release via PRNewswire https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/tata-elxsi-operating-revenue-at-rs-3-729-crores-for-fy25-with-full-year-pbt-at-26-3-302431764.html) on ~12,878 headcount (Q3 FY25, Business Upturn) = ~Rs 29 lakh revenue per employee per year = ~USD 30k at Rs 95.8/USD, implying a blended ~USD 15-18 per billable hour at 1,700-2,000 hours (my derivation; onsite/senior rates will be multiples). VVDN's hardware-engineering page (https://www.vvdntech.com/product-engineering/hardware-engineering), Mistral's resourcing page (https://www.mistralsolutions.com/product-engineering-services/resourcing/ - onsite/offshore blended teams, AXISCADES subsidiary, Bangalore) and Sasken's hardware-design page publish no rates. GAP (c) FY27 status of the wearables PMP duty ladder: NOT FOUND. What surfaced: (i) three CBIC notifications of 8 Jul 2026 extend BCD exemptions on display-assembly parts, smartphone wireless-charging module parts and Li-ion machinery to 2029 but expressly EXCLUDE display assemblies for cellular phones and wrist-wearable devices (India Briefing https://www.india-briefing.com/news/india-customs-duty-exemption-electronics-till-2029-45983.html/); (ii) Notification 33/2023-Customs re-set the graded structure for hearables/wearables after FY23 (https://www.taxtmi.com/notifications?id=140054); (iii) Budget 2026-27 BCD-reform coverage (Sanskriti IAS, ClearTax) showed no wearable-specific line in snippets. CAUTION: a search hit saying 'smart watches to cost more in the 2026-27 budget' is Bangladesh's budget (Daily Star), not India's. Three follow-up searches (ladder table; Budget 2025-26 amendment; post-Mar-2026 PCBA rate) were blocked by the search budget. Needed: current text of 11/2022-Customs as amended (CBIC) to read the FY27 rates for PCBA, cell, charger and mechanics.

The BIS CRS official fee schedule search was blocked by the search budget. Separate CRS on the Li-ion cell/pack under IS 16046 (Part 2):2018 was NOT verified this session (search budget).

UNVERIFIED (search budget): ECMS 'notified 8 Apr 2025' exact date; boAt wearables Rs 330.41 crore / 10.76% of FY25 revenue; IDC overall wearables ASP USD 20.3; Counterpoint Q1 2025 -33%; Ultrahuman 400/day and 1,350/day; WPC ETA '1-3 working days'; Optiemus 14M+ cumulative devices and Harman relationship; BIS IS 16046 (Part 2):2018 battery CRS.

summary: 30 of the planned ~48 searches ran before the session's 200-call WebSearch budget was exhausted; 16 load-bearing claims were checked. Confirmed (10): ECMS outlay/dates/tenure/targets (PIB PRID 2116172), the 20% BCD on finished smartwatches (HS 8517 62 90, plus SWS and IGST), BIS CRS under IS 13252 with the 1 Nov 2028 migration to IS/IEC 62368-1:2023, the Rs 10,000 WPC ETA fee, boAt's UDRHP localisation and Califonix output/capacity, Dixon's Rs 175 crore Q1 FY26 wearables+hearables revenue, IDC's 2025 India numbers (114.2M units, 28.9M smartwatches, ASP USD 26.5), both Counterpoint figures (82% localisation in Q3 2023; -27% in Q2 2025), Ultrahuman's Plano facts and VVDN's 9 plants. Corrected (3): the FX rate is ~Rs 95.8/USD on 14 Sep 2026, not Rs 85 (every USD figure in the lens needs re-basing, ECMS = ~USD 2.39B); the ECMS '31 proposals' is an Aug-2026 tranche with cumulative approvals at 106 projects and Rs 1.15 lakh crore of proposals; Optiemus's >10M units/yr target is a smartphone-plant figure, not wearables capacity. Unverifiable (3): the year-by-year PMP component ladder (instrument 11/2022-Customs as amended by 33/2023 confirmed, rates not retrieved), Ultrahuman's India factory location/capacity (Indore unsupported; only Bengaluru named, by Wikipedia), and the Rs 2-30 lakh tooling range (single vendor blog). Refuted (0). Biggest remaining gaps: no public per-unit India EMS conversion charge for a wearable (RFQ only; a crude Dixon/Califonix triangulation caps EMS revenue near Rs 550/unit including materials), no Indian design-services rate cards (Tata Elxsi revenue/employee implies ~USD 15-18 blended per hour), and the FY27 status of the wearables duty ladder, where the only 2026 signal is that wrist-wearable display assemblies were carved out of the July 2026 CBIC exemption extensions.
